conventions.convention: All small balls are closed norm balls of positive radius; limits are taken as r decreases to zero.

A strong small-ball MAP compares ball mass with the supremum over all Banach-space centers. A Cameron–Martin ratio mode compares limits against each fixed Cameron–Martin center, requires eventually positive denominators, and does not assert a strong MAP.

The Cameron–Martin space E is the Hilbert completion of the covariance quotient, mapped into B by the canonical injection i; the penalty uses the E norm, not the B norm. Degenerate Gaussian laws are allowed.

The posterior theorem assumes AC, HB and countable choice, a finite locally Lipschitz potential on all of B, and a quadratic lower bound with an independently available constant for every positive epsilon. Its posterior is a fixed-data normalized update with D=B.
The counterexample's explicit nonexistence statement requires a nonzero translation-invariant Borel measure finite on every bounded Borel set.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC, HB and countable choice. For the stated centered Borel Gaussian law on a real separable Banach space and any h1,h2 in its covariance Hilbert completion E, μ(closed ball(ih1,r))/μ(closed ball(ih2,r)) tends to exp((‖h2‖E²−‖h1‖E²)/2) as r decreases to zero. The denominator is positive for every r>0.

A strong small-ball MAP has m_r(z)/sup_x m_r(x) tending to 1. A Cameron–Martin ratio mode ih has, for every k in E, eventually positive denominators and an existing limit m_r(ih)/m_r(ik) at least 1; this does not assert the global strong condition.
Under AC, HB and countable choice, for every h in E and r>0, μ({x:‖x−ih‖B≤r})≤μ({x:‖x‖B≤r}).

Under its stated Gaussian and potential hypotheses, 0<Z<∞; I(ih)=Φ(ih)+‖h‖E²/2, extended by +∞ outside iE, attains a finite minimum. For fixed h1,h2 in E, posterior ball ratios tend to exp(I(ih2)−I(ih1)). Its minimizers are exactly the Cameron–Martin ratio modes, without a global strong-MAP claim.

concerns.concern: The Definition constructs the covariance completion and canonical injection, and its Definition references explicitly cite [[def-banach-gaussian-covariance-operator-and-rkhs]], but that supplier is absent from deps. This is an actual prerequisite of the relative-mode branch and should be declared in the dependency graph.

The title and final Counterexample prose claim nonexistence of a locally finite translation-invariant reference, whereas steps 1.2–2.1 explicitly assume finiteness on every bounded Borel set. The stronger conclusion is true, but the reduction is omitted: local finiteness at 0 supplies a finite-mass ball B(0,R); place disjoint balls B((R/2)e_j,R/8) inside it, force their common mass to zero, and use a countable cover by balls of radius R/8. Include that reduction or otherwise justify the locally finite wording.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page inventory and the supplied prior-domain definition and Gaussian-series regularity claim against actual uses. The posterior theorem explicitly specializes the full-mass domain to D=B. The counterexample uses H0=H1=ℓ², weights w_j=1, summable eigenvalues 1/(j(j+1)), supplied independent standard normals, and the Gaussian branch's AC/countable-choice assumptions.

Checked the prerequisite page inventory, exact posterior definition and propriety theorem against the consuming statements and proofs. The Gaussian posterior theorem uses one fixed datum, D=B, a finite continuous potential and the explicit nonnegative integrable envelope max(0,epsilon·t²−M_epsilon).
